voided: priced by pricing pipeline p1, before the relative-width liquidity gate existed. The Hull contract is 6.7-7.7% wide (bid 0.06-0.07 / ask 0.07-0.08) and the p2 gate rejects it at >5%; with that side unfillable the three-way de-vig has no complete book, so the draw is unpriceable too. These two carried the largest EPL 'edges' in the ledger (+206% and +64%) -- a fake edge against a price nobody was offering, which is precisely what liquidity.py exists to stop. Missed by the 2026-09-10 void because that void keyed on model_version, which never moved for soccer.

voided: priced against IN-PLAY quotes. The fixture kicked off at 14:00Z (Kalshi expiry 17:00Z less the measured 3h EPL lag) and this row was written at 15:11Z, ~1h into the match, by a pre-game Elo against a market that had already seen the run of play. The 'edge' is the model's ignorance of the score, not a price discrepancy: both sides bet here had been marked DOWN by the market (Liverpool 0.66->0.52, Chelsea 0.80->0.41). Not a tradeable price and not evidence about the model. Gated off by recommend.partition_in_play.
